# A cluster backend says what survives a restart, and what survives losing a node

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-cluster-persistence`

**This ADR proposes and does not implement.** The change spans two repositories — the SDK type and
its `durability()` method live in `gears-rust`, the capability vocabulary and the projector live
here — and it is written to be argued with before anything moves. Nothing in this document is in the
code.

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

A product asks for a cache and gets one. What it cannot ask is whether the values it writes will
still be there after the process restarts, or after a node is lost — and the SDK gives it no way to
find out, because **no backend states either fact anywhere.**

What the SDK does carry today, verified rather than remembered:

* `CacheFeatures` is two private bools, `watch` and `prefix_watch`
  (`cluster-sdk/src/cache/types.rs`). Neither is about persistence.
* `CacheConsistency` has two values, `Linearizable` and `EventuallyConsistent`. A consistency
  answer, not a durability one.
* `LockFeatures` and `LeaderElectionFeatures` carry one `linearizable` bool each.
* `Ttl::Indefinite` says a value has no expiry. That is about *when a value is removed on purpose*,
  not about whether it survives a process that stops.
* Redis's `durability` option is an **input**: it is read at startup and collapses into
  `CacheConsistency`, and nothing can read it back afterwards.

So the vocabulary a product resolves against — `cluster_cap.linearizable`, `.watch`,
`.prefix_watch` (`crates/gearbox-gdl/src/vocabulary.rs`) — has no member for the question, and
`ClusterProviderDecl` has no field that could answer one.

### The tempting shortcut, and why it is wrong

`ClusterProviderDecl::process_local` looks like the answer and is not. It means *the state lives
inside one process* (`crates/gearbox-ir/src/requirement.rs`), which is a **topology** fact: it is
what makes leader election over an in-memory store elect one leader per replica, which is the
failure `GBX0503` exists to catch. A backend can be process-local and durable (a local file), and
not process-local and entirely volatile (a remote in-memory cache). Reading persistence out of it
would be inferring one axis from another.

This repository has already learned that lesson from the other side. The cluster gear's design
records that a bundled `CapabilityClass { Standalone, Durable, InMemory, Coordination }` **was
removed** because it "collapsed three orthogonal axes (topology, persistence, consistency) into one
fuzzy ordering" (`gears-rust gears/system/cluster/docs/DESIGN.md`, elaborated in that repository's
ADR-007). Any proposal here that re-orders those axes is repeating a mistake with a known cost.

## The scale this proposal withdrew before writing it down

The first draft of this ADR proposed an ordered scale — `Ephemeral < Restartable < Replicated` — and
it is recorded here rather than deleted, because the reason it is wrong is the whole argument.

`Replicated` above `Restartable` asserts an implication that is false. An in-memory replicated store
survives losing one node and loses everything when every process restarts; a single-node store with
an append-only log survives a restart and nothing else. Neither is "more durable" than the other,
and a product that asked for the greater one would silently accept the one it could not use.

That is the same axis-collapsing the bundled enum did, in a new coat.

## Decision

**Two independent facts, plus what they are worth.**

```rust
// cluster-sdk/src/cache/types.rs
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct CacheDurability {
    /// Acknowledged writes are still there after this backend's processes
    /// restart, on the same storage.
    survives_restart: bool,
    /// Acknowledged writes are still there after any one node is lost.
    survives_node_loss: bool,
    /// Which acknowledged writes the two flags above are claims about.
    acknowledged: AckScope,
    /// How the backend knows.
    basis: Basis,
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum AckScope { All, WithoutTtl }

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Basis { Verified, AssertedByOperator, Unknown }
```

Four things rather than one, and each answers a question the other three cannot.

**`survives_restart` and `survives_node_loss` are orthogonal.** Either can hold without the other,
which is the example that killed the scale above, and neither implies the other anywhere in this
design.

**`acknowledged` says which writes the claim covers.** A backend that keeps durable keys and drops
TTL'd ones is making a narrower promise. `Ttl` is already in this vocabulary, so the distinction has
somewhere to live.

**`basis` says how it is known.** Redis reads `appendonly`/`appendfsync` at startup and may be told
rather than able to check; postgres reads `synchronous_standby_names`. The SDK already draws exactly
this line elsewhere: `decide_consistency` takes the operator's hint, the topology finding and what
`CONFIG GET` reported, and answers a `ConsistencyDecision` carrying
`asserted_not_verified` (`redis-cluster-plugin/src/preflight.rs`, both arms exercised in its tests).

It goes further than a flag, and the precedent is worth taking whole: an operator who declares
`durability: fsync_always` against a server that readably contradicts it gets a refusal naming both
the claim and the two values the server reported — while a hint *weaker* than the server's actual
setting is accepted, because under-declaring is safe. A durability claim without that distinction
would be a weaker statement than the consistency one sitting beside it in the same struct.

### One contract, and `CacheFeatures` is not touched

The fact is reached through a new `ClusterCacheBackend::durability()`, beside `consistency()` and
`features()`.

**Adding a field to `CacheFeatures` was considered and rejected**, for a reason in this repository's
own projector rather than in taste: `features_call_flag` (`crates/gearbox-project/src/cluster.rs`)
models exactly `CacheFeatures::new(bool)` and `without_watch()`, and errors on any other arity. A
changed constructor is a coordinated break across both repositories; a new method is a new read.

### Loss of storage is excluded from all of it

A cache facade cannot make a backup statement. A flag quietly meaning "restorable" would be the
third axis this design rejected once already, arriving as a footnote.

### What the providers that exist would declare

Stated as claims somebody can check rather than as a grade:

| | `survives_restart` | `survives_node_loss` | `acknowledged` | `basis` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `standalone` | no | no | — | `Verified` — it is a `HashMap` in this process |
| `postgres` | yes | only with synchronous replication | `All` | `Verified` where `synchronous_standby_names` is readable, else `AssertedByOperator` |
| `redis` | depends on `appendonly`/`appendfsync` | depends on topology | `All` | `Verified` where `CONFIG GET` is permitted, else `AssertedByOperator` or `Unknown` |

Nothing in `standalone`'s Rust says its state dies with the process. That is the clearest argument
that the SDK needs somewhere to say it: the most obviously volatile backend in the corpus is silent
on the subject.

### How a gear asks

The existing surface, two more words in the vocabulary:

```python
cluster.cache(profile = "event-broker",
              capabilities = [cluster_cap.survives_restart])
```

### How the resolver checks it

`ClusterProviderDecl::satisfies` is `required.is_subset(have)` and **stays untouched**. The
projection emits `cluster.cache.survives_restart` and `cluster.cache.survives_node_loss`
independently, from the two independent flags. **No implication between them is encoded anywhere**,
which is the correction this ADR exists to make.

A backend whose `basis` is `AssertedByOperator` still emits the capability: the operator's statement
is the product's to trust or not, and silently discarding it would make an operator-configured
deployment unresolvable for a reason nothing reports. `Unknown` emits nothing.

**When a provider declares nothing**, the descriptor field is absent and **no capability is
emitted**, so such a provider satisfies only a requirement that asks for none. Absence is *not* read
as "ephemeral": that would be an inference about somebody else's backend, which is the mistake this
ADR is about. An SDK older than this contract keeps working and simply cannot answer a durability
requirement.

## The question this ADR does not settle

**`acknowledged` is not in the match.** The two flags become capabilities and the scope does not, so
a backend that keeps durable keys and drops TTL'd ones would satisfy a requirement a gear meant
about *all* its writes.

Two ways out, presented rather than chosen:

* **Put the scope in the requirement.** `cluster_cap.survives_restart` means every acknowledged
  write; a backend declaring `WithoutTtl` does not emit it, and a gear content with the narrower
  promise asks for a separate capability. Precise, and it doubles the vocabulary.
* **Leave it out of matching and report it.** The resolver matches on the flags and the resolution
  *states* the scope, so a narrower promise is visible in the explanation rather than silently
  accepted. Cheaper, and it trusts a reader.

Choosing needs a real case and there is none: no backend in the corpus declares a narrow scope
today. Recording the gap beats inventing a rule for it — the same reason `process_local` is declared
rather than inferred.

## Consequences

### What it costs, from the chain as it stands

* the SDK type and the `durability()` method, in `gears-rust`;
* two consts and two `CACHE_ALL` entries (`crates/gearbox-ir/src/requirement.rs`, where `CACHE_ALL`
  is today `[linearizable, watch, prefix_watch]`);
* two `cluster_cap` members and their match arms (`crates/gearbox-gdl/src/vocabulary.rs`, whose
  namespace lists the same three);
* one new read in `project_backend_capabilities` (`crates/gearbox-project/src/cluster.rs`).

`CacheFeatures` is deliberately untouched, which is what keeps this list short.

### What a product gains

A cache requirement that can say what it needs about restarts, and a resolution that refuses a
backend which cannot promise it — at composition time, in the description, rather than as data
missing after an incident.

### What it does not give

Any statement about backups, about recovery time, or about what happens when storage is lost. Those
are operational facts about a deployment, and a cache facade is the wrong place to assert them.

## Confirmation

Not implemented, so nothing confirms it yet. When it is, the shape of the confirmation is already
set by the claims beside it: a projection test that a declared durability reaches
`ClusterProviderDecl`, a resolver test that the two capabilities are emitted independently and that
neither implies the other, and a test that a provider declaring nothing satisfies only a requirement
asking for nothing.

## Traceability

* Extends `cpt-gearbox-adr-macro-projected-catalogue`: one more fact declared by a backend and
  projected into the catalogue, beside the options schema its Amendment 2026-09-22 added.
* Does **not** amend `process_local` in `crates/gearbox-ir/src/requirement.rs`, and says why: it is
  a topology fact and this is a persistence one.
* Answers nothing in `cpt-gearbox-fr-*` today. No functional requirement asks about durability,
  which is itself part of the context: the question has had no vocabulary to be asked in.
